Paper_Metadata.Paper_Title: Densification, microstructure, and mechanical properties of heat-treated MAR-M247 fabricated by Binder Jetting

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 2.2 Post-processing, HIP, and heat treatments
Section 3.3 Microstructure after sintering and HIP-treatment

Measured_Composition.Note: Composition of consumed powder measured by ICP-MS (Table 1). Ni normalized ≈ 59.72 wt% (Data_Nature: Computed)

Measured_Carbon_After_Sintering.Note: Carbon content after sintering; marginally lower than initial 0.15 wt%

Process_Text.original: Gas-atomized MAR-M247 powder was used as feedstock. Binder Jetting on DMP2500 system with 42 µm layer thickness and ~30 pL droplet volume in ambient atmosphere at room temperature using aqueous binder C20 at Dark 3 saturation (69%). After manufacturing: curing at 200 °C for 8 h, depowdering, thermal debinding at 345 °C for 3 h, sintering at 1320 °C at ~0.1 Pa for 6 h, furnace cooling <20 °C/min.
Process_Text.simplified: Binder Jetting (DMP2500) → curing 200°C/8h → debinding 345°C/3h → vacuum sintering 1320°C/~0.1Pa/6h → furnace cooling

Scaling_Factor.Note: to compensate for shrinkage on sintering

Equipment.Name: H800 SF vacuum furnace (Vacua Therm Ltd.)
Sartorius BP-210S with YDK01 Archimedes kit
Jupiter STA 449 F1 thermal analyzer (Netzsch GmbH)

Structure_Text.original: Equiaxed grains with average grain size of 11.3 µm. γ-matrix with γ'-precipitates of two size fractions: coarser 1–2 µm and finer <1 µm. MC carbides along grain boundaries (M = Hf, W, Ta, Ti). Remaining porosity with irregularly shaped pores of ~1–20 µm.
Structure_Text.simplified: Equiaxed γ-matrix grains (11.3 µm), bimodal γ' precipitates (1–2 µm coarse + <1 µm fine), MC carbides at grain boundaries, residual porosity 1–20 µm

Main_Phase.Description: Ni-based solid solution matrix with Co, W, Cr, Mo solid solution strengthening

Secondary_Phases.Description: Ni₃(Al, Ti) precipitates dispersed in γ-matrix
Primary carbides along grain boundaries; M = Hf, W, Ta, Ti
Secondary_Phases.Note: Confirmed by XRD and EDS; assumed HfC, TaC, TiC, WC per Thermo-Calc

Grain_Size.Note: 20 equally spaced vertical and horizontal line intercepts; no significant difference between directions

Relative_Porosity_Range.Note: Remaining porosity range for as-sintered cuboids, stated in Conclusions section

Texture_or_Orientation.Note: No indications for strong crystallographic texture observed in EBSD pole figures

D50.Note: median particle size at 50% of volume distribution

Properties.Note: Hardness values shown in Fig. 15; specific numerical values for as-sintered condition not reported in text or table. Average increase of ~50 HV0.1 after HIP1 stated.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 3.3 Microstructure after sintering and HIP-treatment

Composition.Note: Same powder composition as Item 01. Composition shared per Section 2.2: same MAR-M247 powder used for all specimens.

Process_Text.original: HIP1 cycle: 1000 bar, 1120 °C, 4 h holding, ~180 °C/min cooling, in argon. Applied to sintered cuboids.

Processing.Note: Prior processing stages (BJ, curing, debinding, sintering) shared with Item 01 per Section 2.2.

Structure_Text.original: After HIP1, γ'-precipitates within γ-grains appear less dense but generally larger. Coarser fraction above 5 µm at expense of finer fraction. Ostwald ripening observed. Average grain size 10.3 µm. Majority of pores removed.
Structure_Text.simplified: Equiaxed γ grains (10.3 µm), coarsened γ' (>5 µm coarse, reduced fine fraction), MC carbides at grain boundaries, near-full densification

Coarse_Fraction_Size.Note: >5 µm; grown at expense of fine fraction (Ostwald ripening)

Secondary_Phases.Description: M = Hf, W, Ta, Ti; along grain boundaries and inside/on rim of former pores

Grain_Size.Note: No noticeable grain growth compared to as-sintered

Texture_or_Orientation.Note: No indications for strong crystallographic texture observed

Properties.Note: Hardness values shown in Fig. 15; specific numerical values not reported in text or table. Average increase of ~50 HV0.1 after HIP1 compared to as-sintered. Variation reduced after HIP.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 3.2 Densification of hexagonal tensile specimens
Section 4.3 Relative density and sources of porosity

Process_Text.original: HIP2 cycle: 1500 bar, 1180 °C, 4 h holding, ~180 °C/min cooling, in argon. Applied to sintered hexagonal tensile specimens.

Processing.Note: Prior processing stages shared with Item 01.

Structure_Text.original: HIP2 condition: density of disperse γ'-precipitates within γ-grains reduced further, size of visible γ'-precipitates smaller compared to HIP1. Coarse fraction not grown extensively; finer fraction even smaller, significantly <1 µm. No significant grain growth expected.
Structure_Text.simplified: γ-matrix, reduced γ' fraction, coarse γ' not grown extensively, fine γ' <1 µm, MC carbides, near-full densification

Secondary_Phases.Note: Reduced mass fraction compared to as-sintered and HIP1; HIP2 temperature (1180 °C) just below γ' stability limit

Vertical_Build.Note: No significant difference between vertical and horizontal build directions; values shown in Fig. 7

Horizontal_Build.Note: See Fig. 7 for individual bar values

Relative_Density_Data.Note: As-sintered density values included as pre-HIP2 baseline for comparison; HIP2 density is the primary data for this item.

Texture_or_Orientation.Note: No significant anisotropy in density or tensile properties between build directions

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 3.4 Microstructural evolution through heat treatments HT 1-4

Process_Text.original: HT1 applied to as-sintered condition: solution treatment 1250 °C for 4 h, age hardening 700 °C for 24 h.

Processing.Note: Heat treatment applied to cuboid specimens in Jupiter STA 449 F1 thermal analyzer in argon.

Structure_Text.original: HT1 on as-sintered: age hardening at 700 °C after solution heat treatment resulted in finest dispersion of γ'. Occasionally γ'-precipitates still present after solution heat treatment.
Structure_Text.simplified: Finest dispersion of γ' after solution + single aging

Secondary_Phases.Note: Finest dispersion after HT1; some undissolved γ' occasionally remained after solution treatment

Properties.Note: Hardness values shown in Fig. 15; specific numerical values not reported in text or table. HT1 and HT2 have similar hardness.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 3.4 Microstructural evolution through heat treatments HT 1-4

Process_Text.original: HT2 applied to as-sintered condition: solution treatment 1250 °C for 4 h, age hardening 1000 °C for 12 h, age hardening 700 °C for 24 h.

Structure_Text.original: HT2 on as-sintered: including double-stage aging, had similar size of γ'-precipitates including a fraction of larger γ'-precipitates. Genuinely bimodal γ'-precipitate distribution.
Structure_Text.simplified: Bimodal γ' distribution with fraction of larger precipitates after double-aging

Secondary_Phases.Note: Bimodal distribution; coarsest γ' dissolved, resulting in genuinely bimodal distribution

Properties.Note: Hardness values shown in Fig. 15; specific numerical values not reported in text or table. Similar hardness to HT1.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 3.4 Microstructural evolution through heat treatments HT 1-4

Process_Text.original: HIP1 + HT1: HIP at 1120 °C, 1000 bar, 4 h in argon. Solution treatment at 1250 °C for 4 h, age hardening at 700 °C for 24 h.

Structure_Text.original: HIP1 + HT1: solution treatment dissolved most γ' but some larger precipitates still present. Finest dispersion of γ' after aging at 700 °C.
Structure_Text.simplified: Finest γ' dispersion after solution + single aging on HIP1 base

Secondary_Phases.Note: Some undissolved larger γ' after solution treatment (HIP1 γ' were larger, slower to dissolve); finest dispersion after 700 °C aging

Properties.Note: Hardness values shown in Fig. 15; specific numerical values not reported in text or table.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 3.4 Microstructural evolution through heat treatments HT 1-4

Process_Text.original: HIP1 + HT2: HIP at 1120 °C, 1000 bar, 4 h in argon. Solution treatment at 1250 °C for 4 h, double-aging at 1000 °C for 12 h and 700 °C for 24 h.

Structure_Text.original: HIP1 + HT2: combining solution treatment with subsequent double-aging, coarsest γ'-precipitates no longer present, leading to genuinely bimodal γ'-precipitate distribution.
Structure_Text.simplified: Genuinely bimodal γ' distribution after solution + double-aging on HIP1 base

Secondary_Phases.Note: Genuinely bimodal distribution; coarsest γ' from HIP1 dissolved by solution treatment

Properties.Note: Hardness values shown in Fig. 15; specific numerical values not reported in text or table.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 3.4 Microstructural evolution through heat treatments HT 1-4

Process_Text.original: HIP1 + HT3: HIP at 1120 °C, 1000 bar, 4 h in argon. Age hardening at 700 °C for 24 h only (no solution treatment).

Structure_Text.original: HIP1 + HT3: age hardening without prior solution treatment leads to coarsening of undissolved γ'-precipitates. Aging at 700 °C did not influence size distribution.
Structure_Text.simplified: Coarsened undissolved γ' from HIP1; no change in size distribution from 700°C aging alone

Secondary_Phases.Note: Coarse γ' from HIP1 still present; 700 °C aging did not change size distribution

Properties.Note: Hardness values shown in Fig. 15; specific numerical values not reported in text or table.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 3.4 Microstructural evolution through heat treatments HT 1-4

Process_Text.simplified: Sintered → HIP1 (1120°C/1000bar/4h) → age 1000°C/12h → age 700°C/24h (no solution treatment, double-aging)
Process_Text.original: HIP1 + HT4: HIP at 1120 °C, 1000 bar, 4 h in argon. Double-aging at 1000 °C for 12 h and 700 °C for 24 h (no solution treatment).

Structure_Text.original: HIP1 + HT4: double-aging without solution treatment resulted in uniformly distributed bi-modal distribution of γ'-precipitates compared to as-sintered condition. Coarse γ' from HIP1 still present, plus two additional size ranges of ~1 µm and submicron.
Structure_Text.simplified: Bimodal γ' distribution from double-aging without solution treatment; coarse γ' retained, additional ~1 µm and submicron fractions

Secondary_Phases.Note: Coarse γ' from HIP1 retained; two additional size fractions ~1 µm and submicron from double-aging

Properties.Note: Hardness values shown in Fig. 15; specific numerical values not reported in text or table. Slightly higher hardness on average than HIP1 alone, similar to HT1-2.

items.Sample_ID: MAR-M247 HIP2 + HT2 (tensile specimens, vertical & horizontal)
Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 4.2 Comparison to conventionally manufactured MAR-M247

Process_Text.original: HIP2 + HT2 for tensile specimens: HIP at 1180 °C, 1500 bar, 4 h in argon. Solution treatment at 1250 °C for 4 h in ambient atmosphere, double-aging at 1000 °C for 12 h and 700 °C for 24 h.

Stage6_HeatTreatment_HT2.Note: Tensile specimens heat-treated in N 7/H furnace in ambient atmosphere

Structure_Text.original: Homogeneously distributed bimodular γ'-structures achieved through solution and double-aging heat treatment (HT2). No significant grain growth expected from HIP2 compared to HIP1 due to grain boundary pinning by carbides.
Structure_Text.simplified: Bimodal γ' distribution, equiaxed grains, MC carbides at grain boundaries, near-full densification

Secondary_Phases.Description: Homogeneously distributed bimodal γ' after HT2
M = Hf, W, Ta, Ti; strong presence along grain boundaries

Test_Condition.Strain_Rate: 400 MPa/min until 0.2% strain, then 10%/min until rupture
Test_Condition.Orientation: independent of build direction (average of vertical and horizontal)

Properties.Note: Average value independent of build direction. No significant anisotropy between vertical and horizontal build orientations. Values shown in Fig. 16 and reported in Conclusions.

Test_Condition.Strain_Rate: 400 MPa/min until 0.2% strain, then 10%/min until rupture
Test_Condition.Orientation: independent of build direction (average of vertical and horizontal)

Properties.Note: Average value independent of build direction. No significant anisotropy. Stress-strain curves showed no indications of necking. Brittle fracture observed.

Test_Condition.Strain_Rate: 400 MPa/min until 0.2% strain, then 10%/min until rupture
Test_Condition.Orientation: independent of build direction (average of vertical and horizontal)

Properties.Note: Average elongation independent of build direction. Maximum elongation increased after HIP2, especially for horizontally built specimens. Considerably lower elongation than MIM and VIC. Brittle fracture; no necking observed.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 4.2 Comparison of resulting microstructure and properties to conventionally manufactured MAR-M247

Process_Text.original: Metal Injection Molding (MIM). HIP at 1185 °C and approx. 170 MPa for 4 h. Heat treatment: 1230 °C for 2 h, 1280 °C for 2 h, 1080 °C for 4 h, 870 °C for 20 h.
Process_Text.simplified: MIM → HIP (1185°C/170 MPa/4h) → multi-step heat treatment

Processing.Note: Process parameters from literature [30]; Fig. 17 caption

Structure_Text.original: Equiaxed grains with sizes comparable to D50 powder particle size 15–20 µm. γ'-precipitates 0.5–1 µm. Finely distributed carbide structures (MC, M₂₃C₆, M₆C) along grain boundaries. Remaining porosity ~2% before HIP.
Structure_Text.simplified: Equiaxed grains 15–20 µm, γ' 0.5–1 µm, MC/M₂₃C₆/M₆C carbides at grain boundaries

Properties.Note: Tensile properties shown in Fig. 17; specific MIM values not reported in text. BJ specimens show 200 MPa higher YS than MIM. No standard deviation reported for MIM.
Tensile properties shown in Fig. 17. UTS reduced by ~200 MPa compared to MIM. No standard deviation reported for MIM.
Considerably higher elongation than BJ specimens shown in Fig. 17. No standard deviation reported for MIM.

Raw_Evidence_Span: Section 4.2 Comparison of resulting microstructure and properties to conventionally manufactured MAR-M247

Process_Text.original: Vacuum Investment Casting (VIC). HIP at 1185 °C and approx. 170 MPa for 4 h. Heat treatment: 1185 °C for 2 h and 871 °C for 20 h.

Processing.Note: Process parameters from literature [45]; Fig. 17 caption

Structure_Text.original: Dendritic structure with relatively large grains (>200 µm). Thick γ'-plates ~5 µm and sub-micron γ' in eutectic pools. Large script-like MC carbides with high aspect ratios up to 40 µm inside grains; M₂₃C₆ at grain boundaries. Remaining porosity ~0.25%.
Structure_Text.simplified: Dendritic, grains >200 µm, γ' plates ~5 µm, script-like MC carbides up to 40 µm

Secondary_Phases.Description: Thick γ'-plates ~5 µm and sub-micron γ' in eutectic pools
Script-like, high aspect ratios, up to 40 µm, inside grains

Properties.Note: BJ specimens show similar YS and UTS compared to VIC shown in Fig. 17. Specific VIC values not reported in text.
Similar to BJ shown in Fig. 17.
Considerably higher elongation than BJ shown in Fig. 17.

Process_Text.original: Sintered at 1320 °C for 6 h. Heat treatment HT2: solution treatment at 1250 °C for 4 h, double-aging at 1000 °C for 12 h and 700 °C for 24 h.

Processing.Note: Same prior processing stages (BJ, curing, debinding, sintering) as Item 01. No HIP applied.

Properties.Note: Values shown in Fig. 16; specific numbers not reported in text. YS and UTS increased slightly after HIP2 compared to sintered+HT2 condition.
Values shown in Fig. 16; specific numbers not reported in text. Larger variation in YS and UTS for horizontally built specimens.
